clue.text: Move a little bit

definitions.meaning: to move someone is to affect them emotionally
a small amount, as in a dash of salt

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to stir someone's feelings, and a tiny trace of something, as in a hint of irony.

clue.text: Try explosive striker for big game

parts.note: to try something is to test it
a match strikes and ignites

explanation.surface: Trying out a powerful forward for an important fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer; it is a match struck on a box. A Test match is an international cricket fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is a major international cricket fixture lasting up to five days.

clue.text: Refusal in university upset student organization

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for refusal is read bottom to top

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A student body is upset when the university refuses something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link, not a container signal. In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so the refusal ends up reading ON beneath the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A students' union is the body that represents and organises students at a college.

clue.text: Arrogance of foreign director after Hollywood opening

indicators.note: after puts the director piece behind the opening letter
opening picks out the first letter of Hollywood

parts.note: auteur is the French term for a film director with a strong personal style

explanation.surface: A European film director shows arrogance after arriving in Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauteur is haughtiness, a proud disdainful manner.

clue.text: Northerners (wrongly?) frustrate king and queen, say

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to thwart or put a stop to it
the king and queen are examples of chess pieces, called men

explanation.surface: Someone bothers a royal couple, and the culprits are said to be people from up north.
explanation.walkthrough: '(wrongly?)' is part of the definition: Scots dislike the word Scotch applied to people rather than whisky, preferring Scotsmen. 'say' marks king and queen as examples of chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Scotland live in the north of Britain, though the form with Scotch is frowned on, hence the setter's query.

clue.text: Among names brought up, there's a Jack

indicators.note: among puts the a inside the reversed names
in a down clue brought up means the word names is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack is among the names mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns NAMES into SEMAN, and A goes 'Among' it. 'there's' is a link; jack is slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack, or Jack tar, is old slang for a sailor.

clue.text: Finished with special plea, that's clear

parts.note: something finished is over

indicators.note: special suggests the letters of plea are put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone done with a special plea finds it costly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'that's' are links; 'special' rearranges PLEA into LEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To overleap is to jump over an obstacle, as a horse clears a fence.

clue.text: Entertainment with some music, a bar, etc.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A night out with some music, a drink at the bar and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a show of songs and acts given in a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: Spy chief and others employ forger's art

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
et al is Latin shorthand for and others
to employ someone is to work them

explanation.surface: The intelligence boss and colleagues use a counterfeiter's skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests a counterfeiter; it is a smith at a forge.
explanation.definitionFit: A forger here is a blacksmith working at a forge, whose craft is shaping iron.

clue.text: One of the locals inhabiting Gotham?

definitions.text: One of the locals inhabiting Gotham?

parts.words: One of the locals inhabiting Gotham?
parts.note: Gotham is not Batman's city but the English village whose people were proverbially foolish, so one of them is a simpleton

explanation.walkthrough: Gotham in Nottinghamshire has an old legend of villagers who feigned stupidity; the question mark marks the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wise Men of Gotham, a Nottinghamshire village, were legendary fools, so a resident is a fool.

clue.text: Pretend to put end of foot in fire

indicators.note: in tells us the foot's last letter is placed inside the word for pretend

parts.note: to simulate is to feign or fake

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word foot

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to fake putting your toes into the flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put' is a link; 'in' puts T, the end of 'foot', into SIMULATE. 'fire' is a verb here, as in fire someone's imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to excite or rouse them, which is what stirring them into action means.

clue.text: Don't declare half of 25's capital

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a side that does not declare its innings closed carries on batting
25 across is a US state whose capital is a two-word city; this is its first word

explanation.walkthrough: Declaring in cricket means a captain ending the team's innings voluntarily; 25 across is LOUISIANA, capital Baton Rouge.
explanation.definitionFit: Batting on is what a cricket side does when it doesn't declare, and Baton Rouge is the capital of Louisiana.

clue.text: Needing motor, nearly call off this car race

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; nearly is not a trimming signal here

explanation.surface: A driver whose car is short of an engine almost calls off the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' tempts you to drop a letter, but all fifteen letters of MOTOR NEARLY CALL are rearranged, signalled by 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monte Carlo Rally is a famous motor rally held around Monaco, an annual car race.

clue.text: Royal line deriving from Stroud

indicators.note: deriving from says the answer's letters are got out of the word that follows by reworking them

parts.note: a town in Gloucestershire, taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal dynasty said to have its origins in a Gloucestershire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroud is a market town in Gloucestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor family were a dynasty of English monarchs from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Frank's in the county side

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
right is one side

explanation.surface: A man called Frank plays in the county team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' is a link; 'Frank's' means Frank is, the definition. Down is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright describes plain, blunt, outspoken speech, the sense of frank.

clue.text: Express fare

parts.note: express means quick, as in an express train
fare is food, as in simple fare

explanation.surface: Food that comes quickly, or perhaps the price of a train ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an express train's ticket price; the whole clue also defines quickly served meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgers and similar meals served quickly over the counter are speedily delivered food.

clue.text: Group of players not allowed, we hear, to go after ball

indicators.note: to go after places the sound-alike piece behind the ball piece

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: we hear means the word for not allowed is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: banned means prohibited

explanation.surface: Sportsmen barred from a match follow the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests sport; they are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance band is a group of musicians playing for dancing.

clue.text: Tree a main log could be taken from

indicators.note: could be taken from signals that the answer is made by reworking the letters of a main log

explanation.surface: A tree from which a main log might be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering tree or shrub with large showy blooms.

clue.text: What comes from a bowler, perhaps, after bad shot, grabbing a wicket

definitions.text: What comes from a bowler, perhaps, after bad shot, grabbing a wicket

indicators.note: after puts the hat piece behind the rest
grabbing means the reworked letters hold the wicket's letter inside them
bad signals that the letters of shot are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
a bowler is one example of a hat

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's cry after a batsman's poor stroke gets him out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the shot into HOST. The surface reads as cricket throughout: the whole clue also describes the appeal a bowler shouts to the umpire after a ball that may have taken a wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the bowler's appeal to the umpire asking whether the batsman is out is the shout 'Howzat'.

clue.text: Disloyalty spelling the end of lost cause

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of lost

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: Betrayal means the end of a lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' is a link, meaning signifying.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country or ruler, the gravest kind of disloyalty.

clue.text: Small part played to make constitutional progress

definitions.meaning: a minor non-speaking role in a play or film
a constitutional is a health walk, so this means to keep going on foot

explanation.walkthrough: A 'constitutional' is an old-fashioned word for a walk taken for one's health; 'constitutional' tempts towards politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit role on stage has that name, and continuing a stroll is to keep walking ahead.

clue.text: Seeking forgiveness, little woman is going into retreat? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: is going into signals one piece entering another
quite the opposite reverses the roles, so the retreat goes into the little woman

parts.note: Amy is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
a nest is a snug retreat

explanation.surface: A small woman seeks forgiveness by withdrawing, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeking' is a link. Read straight, 'is going into' would put the little woman inside the retreat; 'Quite the opposite' swaps the roles, so the retreat sits inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a general pardon granted to offenders.

clue.text: Writing in a certain capacity

definitions.meaning: a book or tome of written work
the amount of space a container holds

explanation.definitionFit: A volume is a book, and also the cubic space something occupies.

clue.text: Awful queen associated, with inane item to eat

definitions.text: Awful queen associated, with inane item to eat

indicators.note: awful signals the letters that follow are mangled

parts.note: R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A queen remembered for a foolish remark about food.
explanation.walkthrough: R plus INANE ITEM TO EAT is rearranged ('Awful'); the whole clue is the French queen linked to 'Let them eat cake', cake being the silly item to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The French queen guillotined in 1793 is popularly credited with suggesting starving peasants eat cake instead of bread.

clue.text: Young boxer, after short time, means to finish off opposition

indicators.note: after puts the puppy piece behind the short time

parts.note: mo is short for moment
a young boxer dog is a pup

explanation.surface: A young fighter soon finishes off his rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter; it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to clear away remaining resistance, as troops do after a battle.

clue.text: Follow some athletic events

definitions.meaning: running races as opposed to field events

explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to track them, and running races are track events.

clue.text: Paper produced from centre in Wapping — Times

indicators.note: centre in picks the middle letter of the word Wapping

parts.note: times or eras are ages

explanation.surface: A newspaper turned out at the Times's base in Wapping, East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced from' is a link. Wapping, in East London, was home to The Times's printing works, which gives the surface its newspaper picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets of paper in a book or newspaper are its leaves, each side being numbered.

clue.text: Girl embracing boy in southern state

indicators.note: embracing means the girl's name wraps around the boy's

parts.note: Louisa is a girl's name
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl hugs a boy somewhere in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state on the Gulf of Mexico, capital Baton Rouge, lies in the Deep South.

clue.text: Monarch includes duck and wine in tasty spread

indicators.note: in places the duck and wine pieces inside the spread

parts.note: pâté is a savoury paste spread on toast
a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A king's buffet includes duck and wine in a tasty pâté.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' and 'and' are links. Tent is a sweet red wine from Spain, mostly seen in crosswords; O for duck comes from cricket's zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a ruler with great power, such as a king or emperor.

clue.text: Joined army at last, given the go-ahead

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the word army

parts.note: to OK something is to approve it, so approved is OKed

explanation.surface: Someone signed up to the army, finally getting permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen yoked together are coupled by a wooden crosspiece, so linked or coupled.
